title: Degenerate hot-lane cascade: targeted slot reclamation, soft-restore and telemetry contracts
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Post-incident follow-up for the 2026-03-08 hosted API GPU depletion event that caused sustained queue buildup and SLO violations. This ticket captures the diagnosis, interim mitigations applied during the incident, and a prioritized action plan to prevent recurrence of cross-pool hot-lane cascades and long-lived slot retention by tenants or batch jobs.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-08 02:14 UTC a combination of an autoscaler cooldown regression and a sudden workload (large-context enterprise image-to-text generation with aggressive prefetching) caused multiple GPU pools to exhaust available slots. Queue depth peaked at ~8.3k across three pools; tail latency SLOs were breached for 47 minutes and 12 tenants experienced degraded throughput. Autoscaler logs showed delayed scale up due to a wrong cooldown override; admission allowed long-running prefetch tasks to hold slots beyond expected lifetimes, amplifying queueing.
timeline: 2026-03-08 02:15 UTC - Pager triggered: hosted-inference GPU pool pressure
2026-03-08 02:20 UTC - Ops increased ephemeral priority, enabled graceful-evict on several tenants
2026-03-08 02:25 UTC - Temporary global soft-throttle applied to prefetching-enabled routes
2026-03-08 02:40 UTC - Autoscaler manual override increased pool capacity; queue began to drain
2026-03-08 03:02 UTC - Incident declared resolved; monitoring left in elevated state for 6 hours
2026-03-09 - Post-incident triage started; initial root cause hypotheses collected
root_causes: Regression: autoscaler cooldown override (runtime-config) was unintentionally set to 900s during a canary deploy, delaying scale-up by ~12 minutes in contested pools
Admission controller policy allowed unmetered prefetch tasks to reserve slots without a short-lived eviction path, leading to long slot residency for some requests
KV-cache pollution and large sequence requests caused previously healthy slots to stay occupied far longer than observed baselines
Insufficient slot-level telemetry: no single metric surfaced 'slot residency time' or per-tenant occupied-slot histogram for rapid triage
mitigations_taken: Reverted autoscaler cooldown config to pre-incident value within 4 minutes of detection
Applied temporary soft-throttle on prefetch-capable routes and reduced prefetch concurrency for enterprise tenants
Triggered manual scaledowns and rebalanced a subset of tenants to less-contested pools
Created urgent dashboard showing pool queue length, per-tenant occupied slots, and tail residency percentiles
action_items: Implement per-slot telemetry (slot_residency_ms histogram, tenant_slot_count gauge) and wire into Console alerts - owner: Asha Patel - estimate: 3 - due: 2026-03-20

Add tenant-aware reservation decay: automatically degrade reservation weight for slots held > threshold and migrate long-resident KV-cache items to cold-tier - owner: Daniel Park - estimate: 5 - due: 2026-03-27
Introduce a soft-preempt mechanism that allows low-priority prefetches to be reclaimed after N seconds with graceful retry semantics - owner: Priya Singh - estimate: 8 - due: 2026-04-02
Harden autoscaler config pipeline: add CI check for cooldown overrides and a safe-guard gating deploys that touch autoscaler defaults - owner: Marco Ruiz - estimate: 3 - due: 2026-03-18

Create a synthetic load test reproducer that simulates enterprise long-context + prefetch traffic and run nightly on staging to validate admission controls - owner: Liam Chen - estimate: 5 - due: 2026-03-24
Run a chaos experimentation week (directed chaos) on non-prod GPU pools to validate soft-preempt and reservation-decay behavior - owner: Reliability Team - estimate: 3 - due: 2026-03-31
comments: 2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz: Initial ticket created after triage meeting. Major priority is telemetry and a reclamation path to avoid long-lived slot anchors.
2026-03-11 Asha Patel: Scoped telemetry fields and added a Console mock for slot_residency_ms. Need backend API for per-slot annotations (will design low-risk schema).

2026-03-11 Priya Singh: Draft design for soft-preempt posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/soft-preempt-design. Key risk is client-visible retries for higher-latency requests.

2026-03-12 Daniel Park: Reservation-decay proposal reviewed; suggests a two-tier approach: gradual weight reduction + cold cache eviction. Linked PR for cache eviction logic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4578
2026-03-13 Marco Ruiz: Prioritized action items and set due dates. Will coordinate cross-team design review on 2026-03-17.
acceptance_criteria: Slot residency telemetry available in Console and enabled in staging alerts
Soft-preempt implemented behind a feature flag and validated under synthetic load with <10% client error increase
Autoscaler config CI prevents cooldowns > 300s without explicit multi-owner approval
Nightly repro confirms system no longer exhibits >5k queue depth under enterprise-like prefetch workload in staging
next_steps: Design review (2026-03-17) for soft-preempt and reservation-decay
Telemetry spike to produce slot_residency_ms samples in staging (owner: Asha) by 2026-03-18
Kick off synthetic load test PR and schedule nightly runs (owner: Liam) by 2026-03-20
notes: This incident surfaced a class of cascading degradation where configuration regressions and tenant workload interactions amplify one another. Fixes should prioritize observability + safe reclamation over aggressive global throttles to preserve customer experience while keeping capacity stable.
